note: The Algorithms knowledge library (#2760) — RUST-first, PRIMITIVES-ROOTED, impl-is-concept (#2961): each language is a tier of IMPLEMENTATIONS rooted in that language's PRIMITIVES (role: primitive — Vec, slice, Iterator, Option, HashMap, VecDeque, BinaryHeap, i64, bool, tuple), with algorithms (role: algorithm) composing UP from them; the implementation IS the concept — there is NO abstract concept ontology (nodes/edges/concept removed #2961). The ONE source of truth read by BOTH the frontend (src/features/algorithms) AND the `bsc graph` CLI (crates/bsc-graph embeds it). Each impl: { id, tech, role, name, summary, composes, code }.

implementations.name: groupTotals
implementations.summary: Group rows by a key and total a set of numeric FIELDS — per group AND overall — in ONE pass. The back half of every 'spend by X' rollup. The fields to sum are DATA (a record of named numeric accessors), so adding a tracked metric is one entry, not editing three reducers. Group subtotals and the grand total come from the SAME traversal, so they cannot drift apart — the bug the hand-written three-separate-reductions version has. Groups in first-seen order (the one order needing no opinion; a caller wanting another sorts the result). Harvested from the Fleet page's cost panel (#3462/#3465), rolling per-worker token usage up to fleet totals + a by-model breakdown.

implementations.name: estimateEnergyWh
implementations.summary: Estimate the energy (Wh) an LLM call costs from the model name and its input/output token split: classify the model into a tier by name pattern, then apply per-1k-token coefficients. Directional, not metered — unknown hosted models fall to the mid tier rather than zero, so an unrecognised model is never free. Harvested from the Fleet page's cost panel (#3462).

implementations.name: orderByRank
implementations.summary: Sort items by a DECLARED priority ranking of a category — an order deliberately NOT the category's natural/alphabetical one (an attention queue: by urgency, which no property of the state gives you). The ranking is DATA (an array, first = highest), not magic numbers buried in a comparator's ternary chain where the priority cannot be read as a list or reordered without recounting. An UNRANKED category sorts AFTER every ranked one, not to rank 0 — unranked is 'no stated priority', not 'top priority', the trap the `?? 0` hand-version falls into. Stable within a rank; decorate-sort-undecorate so the category is derived once per item, not per comparison. Harvested from the Fleet page's merge queue (#3462/#3465).

implementations.name: resolveByPrecedence
implementations.summary: Resolve ONE state from N independent signal sources by a DECLARED precedence order, first match wins, sources consulted lazily. The ordering is data rather than control flow: the usual form is a chain of `if` returns where the precedence exists only in statement order and cannot be read, tested or reordered without editing branches. Total by construction (a fallback is required, so there is no resolved-to-nothing case). `matchingPrecedence` returns every rule that claimed the subject, not just the winner — the winner answers "what is it?", the rest is what an explanation needs. Harvested from the Fleet page's per-worker status (#3462/#3465).

implementations.name: mergeFeeds
implementations.summary: Merge K differently-shaped event streams into ONE recent-first feed, with a distinguished class PINNED above the time sort, plus a count per kind. Each stream carries its own projection to a common item so the merge never sees the source shapes — adding a stream is a (source, project) pair, not editing a growing sort. The pin is a real flag, not the `sortKey: Infinity` sentinel the harvested code used (two Infinity items compare to NaN and their order is undefined). Counts come from the merged feed in one pass, so the badge can never disagree with the list. Stable within a rank. Harvested from the Fleet page's health panel (#3462/#3465).

windowedTally
implementations.summary: Bucket K timestamp streams into per-day counts over a rolling N-day UTC window, aligned to one label axis. Two properties are the point: EMPTY DAYS ARE PRESENT (the window is built first and streams tally into it, where deriving labels from the data silently compresses quiet days out of the axis and makes a gap look like a dip), and THE SERIES ARE ALIGNED (every series has one entry per label, in order, so index i means the same day in all of them — a chart layering two series cannot check this). UTC because a window whose bucket boundaries move with the viewer's timezone makes the same data tell two stories. Harvested from the Fleet page's throughput panel (#3462/#3465).
